A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HumanVBench and its benchmark-construction pipelines. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison. The revised benchmark and settings limit direct performance comparisons, rather than document comparability.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 22 MLLMs, human performance, speaker-emotion and timestamp experiments, generation-quality measurements, and an appendix modality ablation.

after.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 30 MLLMs, annotator agreement, distractor-quality analysis, frame-sampling and human-density experiments, and pipeline-transfer examples.

M1.justification: v2 selects answers through sequential pairwise comparisons against the current best answer. v3 replaces this with ensemble ranking and weighted score aggregation, giving Gemini twice the weight of other models (Section 3.3; Appendix L.1). Generation models also change, including GPT-4 replacing Qwen2.5 for question/distractor generation. Section 4.5 additionally implements detector substitutions for non-human tasks.

E1.justification: The 16 human-centric tasks remain, but v3 adds MF2 movie footage alongside Pexels material; Figure 6 now includes a 21% movie category. Section 4.5 and Figure 5 also demonstrate question generation for dogs, vehicle tracking, and animated object-centric causal events. These extend represented domains, although the non-human coverage consists of qualitative demonstrations.

E2.justification: The full performance comparison expands from 22 to 30 models. Added models include InternVideo2.5, ViLAMP, InternVL3/3.5, Qwen3-VL, MIO, Qwen2.5-Omni, GPT-5, and Gemini-2.5-Flash/Pro. PLLaVA and Otter-V disappear from the performance table, despite remaining in the configuration table. The speaking-subset comparison also changes its participating models.

E3.justification: The benchmark changes from 2,116 to 2,475 questions, with revised task counts and a stated maximum duration increasing from 10 to 30 seconds. Reported Qwen2-VL/Qwen2.5-VL sampling changes from eight frames to two frames per second. New protocols include 4/8/16-frame comparisons, density-stratified evaluation, and no-edit/efficiency measurements. These establish changed reported settings, not necessarily rerunning every retained result.

E4.justification: v3 adds distractor-selection analysis, frame-sampling sensitivity, human-density robustness, annotator-agreement validation, and non-human transfer case studies. It revises the speaking-emotion analysis while removing v2's three-category Gemini error breakdown. The modality ablation retains its speech-visual results but drops the other twelve task columns (Table 5 in both versions).

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging open-source model results over five runs with different seeds. v3 newly reports Cohen's kappa of 0.8833 from two independent annotators on 240 randomly sampled questions (Section 3.3). This adds statistical agreement reporting without establishing an increase in model-evaluation runs.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added: VideoLLaMA3's ER accuracy changes from 39.4% to 34.6% on the revised benchmark, and Qwen2.5-Omni newly records 71.8% on SCM. Reported correct-option availability changes from approximately half of generated questions to a 72.3% no-edit rate. New robustness and validation findings further expand the evidence; these are not uniformly comparable-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 newly defines the efficiency-gain quantity as 1 / (1 - No Edit Rate) in Table 2c. This is a limited mathematical definition accompanying a new empirical measure. The face-to-body matching equation remains unchanged, and neither version presents a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The benchmark, automated pipelines, reusability, reduced annotation effort, and remaining human–model gaps are already claimed in v2. v3 more explicitly limits the benchmark's target to foundational perception and strengthens the efficiency claim to multiplied production throughput. Its promotion of a generalizable construction framework partly reframes transferability already claimed in v2.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive interpretations linking crowding failures primarily to person localization, dense sampling to diminishing returns and temporal redundancy, and distractor-selection distributions to discriminatory difficulty. It also qualifies the earlier broad account of weak open-source audio-visual performance by identifying Qwen2.5-Omni as an exception. These extend the retained speaking-emotion and modality explanations.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation changes materially: v3 supplies revised ranking prompts, aggregation weights, generation-model choices, object-detector adaptations, and expanded configuration/runtime entries. Conversely, its configuration table removes VRAM measurements, and Appendix L.3 omits the human-baseline calculation described in v2 Section 12.3. Most detailed task-construction templates remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the broad MLLM overview with substantially expanded positioning around foundational perception, emotion datasets, social reasoning, benchmark construction, and distractor generation. Newly discussed work includes VEATIC, Social-IQ, MotionBench, and distractor-generation methods. Appendix B/Table 3 adds a structured comparison with existing benchmarks, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the methodology and evaluation narrative are rewritten. Task descriptions and pipeline subsections are compressed and reorganized; analyses are regrouped; and the appendix gains a contents list and lettered organization. These are extensive narrative changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the answer-generation diagram, replaces the main detailed results matrix with a summary while moving full results to the appendix, and consolidates analyses into Table 2a–c. It replaces the generation-quality chart with a table and adds transfer examples, a distractor histogram, and analysis tables. Most appendix task illustrations are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the agreement study and distractor analysis strengthen support for benchmark reliability, while sampling and crowding experiments improve diagnostic value. These gains outweigh the loss of human-baseline and VRAM documentation, but the overall improvement is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix D still says 24 models despite reporting 30, and Table 1's Gemini-2.5-Flash overall average disagrees with its category means.
